title: Officer charged with assault, relieved of duties
article: A New Westminster police officer already facing a wrongful-death lawsuit has been relieved of his duties following charges of assault causing bodily harm in a separate incident.
Const. Todd Sweet was suspended with pay on Tuesday over an incident in which he is alleged to have kicked a car-theft suspect in the head while the suspect was wearing handcuffs.
Sweet, a 16-year veteran of the New Westminster Police Service and a spokesman for the B.C. Federation of Police Officers, was charged on Tuesday by Abbotsford police after an 18-month investigation.
The incident in question happened in June 2005 when police captureda man, 29after a chase.
New Westminster police Chief Lorne Zapotichny said he learned about the allegations in an anonymous letter sent two weeks after the alleged incident.

Several weeks later,Sweet shot and killed Kyle Tait, 16, who was a passenger in a stolen SUV being chased by police.Sweet has said the driver in the August 2005 incident was trying to use the SUV as a weapon.
The officer was put on desk duty after Tait was killed.
Tait's family has filed a wrongful-death lawsuit against Sweet, claiming the vehicle the teen was in was not moving when the officer fired.

In another development, according to the Globe and Mail, a confidential settlement was reached in June between William Harris, a lawyer, and the City of New Westminster over the alleged conduct of Sweet from an incidentin October 1999.

Mr. Harris claimed he suffered a separated shoulder and perforated eardrum after a confrontation with the officer, the paper reported. A 70-year-old from Burnaby has also filed an excessive-force complaint against Sweet.
